notes: Main disagreements: (1) modality, where A used should or informs and B informs or must on sentences such as 'must maximize opportunities' and the 'ideal human-centered practices' list; resolved to the source's own wording (must) and to should for items in the recommended-practices list. (2) actor: all vs instructor/student, and admin vs instructor on the detection best practices ('Instructors should adopt...') and on the four syllabus approaches; resolved to instructor where the source addresses instructors or offers the option to faculty. (3) policy_type on the Use with Acknowledgement sentence (P02 vs P24, resolved to P24 because the cite-or-acknowledge condition carries the rule), the citation-format sentence (P24 vs P25, resolved to P25), and the 'grasp the boundaries, risks' sentence (UNCOVERED vs P31, resolved to P31). (4) phase on the syllabus advice and the Use with Permission option. (5) Splitting: B split out the four definitions, the autonomy practice, the rooted-in-the-course sentence, the detector advantages, the Turnitin and K-16 access statements and several explain-the-reasons sentences; all are real statements and were kept (17). B's opening provenance sentence (developed in 2024 by the committee) was dropped as authorship metadata, not a policy. A had no unmatched units. Stance matched (delegates). new_types empty on both sides; A's one UNCOVERED unit was mapped to P31.
